# ERP isolated commercial UAT — 2026-09-29

Source checkout HEAD: `085d0cebb6aefd3152e475e8337ff988a281f5ff`. The existing commercial setup, workflow, config, loader, and Keycloak setup files in the archive copy were SHA-256 identical to the source checkout. No source assertions or product code were edited. The only added test file was `/tmp/harness-multiproject-qa/erp/frontend/playwright.qa-commercial.config.ts` (SHA-256 `6a2ba658724dd070682d5257f27cb4b5490fec967939949f4323989859b9cf5c`), selecting the existing UAT projects, an already running frontend on port 53186, one worker, and a 180-second timeout.

Isolation and identity: dedicated `harness-qa-erp-pg` PostgreSQL 16.14 was confirmed via Docker label `harness.qa=20260929`, loopback port `127.0.0.1:55436`, database and user `erp_qa`, with no mounts. An isolated `harness-qa-erp-kc` Keycloak 26 container used label `harness.qa=20260929`, loopback port `127.0.0.1:58186`, and tmpfs data. Backend ran from the copied `erp-backend-0.13.0.jar` on port 58086 with the default (security enabled) Spring profile and Keycloak issuer `http://localhost:58186/realms/erp`. Frontend BFF ran from the copied build on loopback port 53186. Explicit local-only fixture credentials were used; existing `.env` contents were not read. `E2E_COMMERCIAL_MUTATION=LOCAL_MUTATION_ACCEPTED` was supplied only after confirming the dedicated DB identity. No remote systems or paid APIs were used.

Execution evidence:

1. Parent-owned `./gradlew --offline --no-daemon check bootJar`: 936/936 passing per `/tmp/harness-integration-erp/backend-check.json` and `logs/backend-check.log` (not rerun here).
2. Existing `scripts/keycloak-setup.sh` against dedicated Keycloak: exit 0; sanitized `keycloak-setup.log`. The original script prints ephemeral client secrets, so its raw private log is not included in the final evidence set.
3. Backend default profile: health HTTP 200, Flyway validated 42 migrations, schema current at version 4005; `backend-runtime.log` and `backend-health.json`.
4. `npm run build` with explicit local fixture environment: initial sandbox run exit 1 because Next could not fetch the public Geist fonts; approved network run exit 0. `frontend-build.log` contains the successful run; the first failure was observed in tool output. Frontend `/login` HTTP 200.
5. Existing `commercial.setup.ts` through the QA Playwright config: exit 0, 1/1 passed in 26.9 seconds (`commercial-setup.log`). It provisioned the two UAT tenants and four user identities through actual Keycloak and the Gradle provisioning task.
6. Existing `commercial-workflow.spec.ts` through the same config with `--no-deps` because setup had already passed: exit 0, 3/3 passed in 7.5 seconds (`commercial-workflow.log`). Covered AP/AR → GL/reports/VAT, inventory movement and approval with audit trace, and browser CSV/low-privilege/expired-session behavior.
7. Post-run DB observation: `common.tenant` included `UAT_A` and `UAT_B` and `common.tenant_user` contained 10 rows; this count includes earlier QA fixtures from the parent-owned backend check, so it is not solely attributable to this UAT.

Verdict: **PASS** for this isolated local Keycloak/PG/API/BFF commercial UAT. Scope limits: no deployed environment, no real customer identities, and no multi-instance runtime or production configuration. The backend listened on all local interfaces while active; it is stopped after the run.

Cleanup: the verified backend/frontend listener PIDs were terminated, both dedicated Docker containers were removed with volumes, and subsequent listener/container checks returned no matches. The private local credential file and raw Keycloak output were removed; the redacted setup log remains.

# DriveTree isolated integration QA — 2026-09-29

Source: `/Users/grinvi04/project/DriveTree` HEAD `ab86d1394b3b52b8acb56a794854ce49995f5c21`. The five relevant source/test files in the archive copy had identical SHA-256 hashes to the source checkout. No source or harness files were edited. The extra probe was written only to `/tmp/harness-multiproject-qa/DriveTree/backend/test/qa-http-boundary.e2e-spec.ts` (SHA-256 `759366ed58ca06e3791588e354eede3be8985cb4558ae0238eb07f2b1547c2a7`).

Isolation: `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` in `harness-qa-drivetree-20260929`, label `harness.qa=20260929`, bound only to `127.0.0.1:55434`, no host bind mounts. Docker created one anonymous database volume for the container. Database `drivetree_qa` and dummy credentials were created for this run. `GEMINI_API_KEY=''`; no external Gemini call. No `.env` contents were read. Source fixture `deleteMany` operations ran only against this disposable database. The HTTP probe used the real `AppModule`, guards, pipes, filter, cache interceptor, and Nest HTTP server through Supertest; it did not test a separately deployed listener.

Cleanup: `docker rm --force --volumes harness-qa-drivetree-20260929` exited 0. Follow-up Docker list checks found neither that container nor its anonymous volume.

Commands and results:

1. `npm exec prisma migrate deploy` under a clean explicit environment targeting only `postgresql://qa:dummysecret@127.0.0.1:55434/drivetree_qa?schema=public`: exit 0, three migrations applied. Log: `migration.log`. An initial sandboxed call could not reach localhost (P1001); the approved escalated call succeeded.
2. `npm run test:e2e -- --runInBand` in `backend` under the same database environment and with blank Gemini key: exit 0, 4 suites and 13 tests passed. Log: `e2e.log`.
3. Full AppModule HTTP probe, initial creation cache experiment: exit 1. Anonymous `GET /api/content?search=qadrivetreekeyword` cached an empty result before admin POST. A subsequent successful admin POST did not appear at the same search URL. Log: `http-boundary.log`.
4. HTTP probe with the creation cache key separated: exit 1, 2 passed and 1 failed. Admin creation and public lookup passed; after deletion, the pre-warmed search URL still returned the deleted ID. Log: `http-boundary-delete.log`.
5. Final HTTP probe: exit 1, 3 passed and 1 failed. Anonymous POST/PATCH/DELETE and invalid login returned 401; authorized admin login/POST/PATCH/DELETE and anonymous GET returned expected success. After deletion, the DB row had `deletedAt`, embeddings remained, ID and slug reads returned 404, and a previously unused search URL excluded the deleted ID. The pre-warmed search URL still returned it (the failed assertion). After 61 seconds, that same URL excluded it (passing assertion). Log: `http-boundary-final.log`.

Verdict: existing DB E2E **PASS**; HTTP authorization checks **PASS** in the tested cases; immediate HTTP list/search consistency after writes **FAIL**. The likely cause is `ContentController`'s `CacheInterceptor` with `@CacheTTL(60_000)` and no invalidation in `ContentService.create/update/remove`. This is a cause hypothesis from the source and behavior, not a product-code fix.

Missing cases: cookie-only auth and refresh, production listener/CORS, a non-admin authenticated role, real Gemini embeddings and semantic vector search, concurrent writes, cache behavior across multiple server instances, and full expiry timing around the exact 60-second boundary were not verified. The only checked expiry point was 61 seconds. The original 13 E2E tests exercise the local NLP fallback and DB persistence, not paid Gemini paths.

The supported endpoints were checked in `ApInvoiceController` (`POST /api/finance/invoices/{id}/cancel`) and `ItemController` (`DELETE /api/inventory/items/{id}`), plus their service behavior and `INVOICE_NOT_FOUND` / `ITEM_NOT_FOUND` 404 error definitions.

New assertions executed against real Bearer tokens and API/database state:

| Tenant B attempt | Precondition | Denial | Tenant A state after request |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/finance/invoices/1/cancel` | B has `finance:write`; A invoice is `DRAFT` | HTTP 404 | Entire owner invoice response equals before; `status=DRAFT`, `invoiceNo=AP-CBC5DF74`, `totalAmount=11000`, `journalEntryId=null` |
| `DELETE /api/inventory/items/1` | B has `inventory:write`; A item is active | HTTP 404 | Entire owner item response equals before; `name=UAT 상품 CBC5DF74`, `active=true`, `version=0` |

The checks run before the normal AP submit and inventory movement steps, so a business lifecycle restriction cannot explain these 404 results. The permissions checks guard against a denial caused merely by missing write privileges.

Execution: `commercial-cross-setup.log` shows existing setup **1/1 passed**; `commercial-cross-workflow.log` shows the whole existing three-test UAT, including these additions, **3/3 passed**. Workflow ran with `--no-deps` after setup passed separately. Rebuilt frontend with the new local client secret, exit 0 (`frontend-cross-build.log`). No full backend check rerun was needed; the first run's parent-owned 936/936 evidence remains in `backend-check.json`.

Scope limit: frontend BFF browser cookies in `commercial-workflow.spec.ts` are synthetically encoded with `@auth/core/jwt`; they are not created by an interactive Keycloak browser login. The expired-session test changes client session metadata and supplies an invalid refresh token; it does not demonstrate backend rejection of an expired access JWT. The cross-tenant write probes above use real Keycloak Bearer access tokens against the backend, independent of that browser-cookie shortcut.

Cleanup: both verified backend/frontend listener PIDs and both dedicated containers were terminated; subsequent listener and Docker checks returned no matches. The temporary credential file and raw Keycloak output were removed. `keycloak-setup-cross.log` retains redacted setup evidence.

import { Test } from '@nestjs/testing'
import { INestApplication, ValidationPipe } from '@nestjs/common'
import request from 'supertest'
import cookieParser from 'cookie-parser'
import { AppModule } from '../src/app.module'
import { PrismaService } from '../src/prisma.service'
import { AllExceptionsFilter } from '../src/common/all-exceptions.filter'

describe('QA: full HTTP content/auth boundary', () => {
  let app: INestApplication
  let prisma: PrismaService
  let token: string
  let id: string
  const slug = 'qa-drivetree-auth-delete'
  const payload = {
    title: 'QA sample driving rule',
    slug,
    content: 'Unique qadrivetreekeyword content for isolated integration verification.',
    category: 'rules',
    tags: ['qadrivetreekeyword'],
  }

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const moduleRef = await Test.createTestingModule({ imports: [AppModule] }).compile()
    app = moduleRef.createNestApplication({ logger: false })
    app.setGlobalPrefix('api')
    app.use(cookieParser())
    app.useGlobalFilters(new AllExceptionsFilter())
    app.useGlobalPipes(new ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, transform: true }))
    await app.init()
    prisma = app.get(PrismaService)
  })

  afterAll(async () => {
    if (id) {
      await prisma.contentEmbedding.deleteMany({ where: { contentId: id } })
      await prisma.content.deleteMany({ where: { id } })
    }
    await prisma.$disconnect()
    await app.close()
  })

  it('denies anonymous writes and invalid login, while allowing anonymous reads', async () => {
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).get('/api/content?search=qaotherkeyword').expect(200)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).post('/api/content').send(payload).expect(401)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).patch('/api/content/unknown').send({ title: 'New' }).expect(401)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).delete('/api/content/unknown').expect(401)
    await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .post('/api/auth/login')
      .send({ username: 'qaadmin', password: 'incorrect-password' })
      .expect(401)
  })

  it('allows authenticated admin write and public read', async () => {
    const login = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .post('/api/auth/login')
      .send({ username: 'qaadmin', password: 'dummysecret-admin' })
      .expect(200)
    token = login.body.accessToken as string
    expect(token).toBeTruthy()
    const created = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .post('/api/content')
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send(payload)
      .expect(201)
    id = created.body.id as string
    expect(id).toBeTruthy()
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).get(`/api/content/${id}`).expect(200)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).get(`/api/content/slug/${slug}`).expect(200)
    const search = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .get('/api/content?search=qadrivetreekeyword')
      .expect(200)
    expect(search.body.data.map((item: { id: string }) => item.id)).toContain(id)
    await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .patch(`/api/content/${id}`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .send({ title: 'Updated QA sample' })
      .expect(200)
  })

  it('excludes soft-deleted item from public item and cached search endpoints', async () => {
    await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .delete(`/api/content/${id}`)
      .set('Authorization', `Bearer ${token}`)
      .expect(200)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).get(`/api/content/${id}`).expect(404)
    await request(app.getHttpServer()).get(`/api/content/slug/${slug}`).expect(404)
    const row = await prisma.content.findUnique({ where: { id } })
    expect(row?.deletedAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date)
    expect(await prisma.contentEmbedding.count({ where: { contentId: id } })).toBeGreaterThan(0)
    const uncached = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .get('/api/content?search=qadrivetreekeyword&category=rules')
      .expect(200)
    expect(uncached.body.data.map((item: { id: string }) => item.id)).not.toContain(id)
    const search = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .get('/api/content?search=qadrivetreekeyword')
      .expect(200)
    expect(search.body.data.map((item: { id: string }) => item.id)).not.toContain(id)
  })

  it('returns current search results after the 60-second cache TTL', async () => {
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 61_000))
    const search = await request(app.getHttpServer())
      .get('/api/content?search=qadrivetreekeyword')
      .expect(200)
    expect(search.body.data.map((item: { id: string }) => item.id)).not.toContain(id)
  }, 70_000)
})

import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import time
from unittest.mock import patch

import redis
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import select

import app.database
import app.main
from app.dependencies import get_current_user
from app.models.customer import Customer
from app.models.webhook_event import WebhookEvent


def signature(body: bytes, secret: str) -> str:
    return "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def count_for(customer_id, event_id):
    with app.database.SessionLocal() as db:
        return len(
            db.scalars(
                select(WebhookEvent).where(
                    WebhookEvent.customer_id == customer_id,
                    WebhookEvent.event_id == event_id,
                )
            ).all()
        )


def await_count(customer_id, event_id, expected):
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        count = count_for(customer_id, event_id)
        if count == expected:
            return
        time.sleep(0.15)
    raise AssertionError(f"count expected {expected}, observed {count}")


def post(client, tenant, secret, delivery):
    body = json.dumps(
        {
            "action": "opened",
            "sender": {"login": "qa"},
            "repository": {"full_name": "qa/example"},
        }
    ).encode()
    return client.post(
        f"/webhooks/{tenant}/github",
        content=body,
        headers={
            "content-type": "application/json",
            "X-Hub-Signature-256": signature(body, secret),
            "X-GitHub-Delivery": delivery,
        },
    )


def main():
    with app.database.SessionLocal() as db:
        a = Customer(tenant_id="qa-tenant-a", name="A", webhook_secret="qa-secret-a", allowed_event_types=[])
        b = Customer(tenant_id="qa-tenant-b", name="B", webhook_secret="qa-secret-b", allowed_event_types=[])
        db.add_all([a, b])
        db.commit()
        a_id, b_id = a.id, b.id

    r = redis.Redis.from_url("redis://127.0.0.1:56379/0")
    assert r.ping()
    with TestClient(app.main.app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
        first = post(client, "qa-tenant-a", "qa-secret-a", "qa-dup")
        duplicate = post(client, "qa-tenant-a", "qa-secret-a", "qa-dup")
        wrong_tenant_secret = post(client, "qa-tenant-b", "qa-secret-a", "qa-bad")
        other_tenant = post(client, "qa-tenant-b", "qa-secret-b", "qa-dup")
        assert (first.status_code, duplicate.status_code, wrong_tenant_secret.status_code, other_tenant.status_code) == (202, 202, 401, 202)
        assert duplicate.json()["message"] == "Webhook already processed."
        await_count(a_id, "qa-dup", 1)
        await_count(b_id, "qa-dup", 1)
        print("PASS actual worker + PostgreSQL + Redis: duplicate reservation, tenant key separation, signature isolation, one row each")

        key = "webhook:idempotency:qa-tenant-a:github:qa-retry"
        with patch("app.main.get_task") as task_lookup:
            task_lookup.return_value.apply_async.side_effect = RuntimeError("injected enqueue failure")
            failed = post(client, "qa-tenant-a", "qa-secret-a", "qa-retry")
        assert failed.status_code == 500, failed.text
        assert not r.exists(key)
        retried = post(client, "qa-tenant-a", "qa-secret-a", "qa-retry")
        assert retried.status_code == 202, retried.text
        await_count(a_id, "qa-retry", 1)
        assert r.exists(key)
        print("PASS injected broker-enqueue failure: 500, reservation released, actual retry processed once")

        # Force a second broker delivery after the Redis reservation is gone;
        # PostgreSQL's uniqueness constraint must still prevent a second effect.
        r.delete("webhook:idempotency:qa-tenant-a:github:qa-dup")
        redelivered = post(client, "qa-tenant-a", "qa-secret-a", "qa-dup")
        assert redelivered.status_code == 202
        time.sleep(1)
        assert count_for(a_id, "qa-dup") == 1
        print("PASS actual redelivery after Redis key deletion: PostgreSQL backstop kept one row")

        with app.database.SessionLocal() as db:
            a_event = db.scalars(select(WebhookEvent).where(WebhookEvent.customer_id == a_id, WebhookEvent.event_id == "qa-dup")).one()
            a_event_id = a_event.id
            assert a_event.status == "PROCESSED"

        anonymous = client.post(f"/webhooks/qa-tenant-a/events/{a_event_id}/replay")
        assert anonymous.status_code == 401
        app.main.app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: {"preferred_username": "qa-user", "realm_access": {"roles": ["user"]}}
        forbidden = client.post(f"/webhooks/qa-tenant-a/events/{a_event_id}/replay")
        assert forbidden.status_code == 403
        app.main.app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: {"preferred_username": "qa-admin", "realm_access": {"roles": ["admin"]}}
        cross_tenant = client.post(f"/webhooks/qa-tenant-b/events/{a_event_id}/replay")
        assert cross_tenant.status_code == 404
        owner = client.post(f"/webhooks/qa-tenant-a/events/{a_event_id}/replay")
        assert owner.status_code == 202, owner.text
        app.main.app.dependency_overrides.clear()
        print("PASS actual PostgreSQL replay lookup: anonymous 401, user 403, cross tenant 404, admin owner 202")

    r.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Force a real Kombu connection failure after a real Redis idempotency reservation."""

import hashlib
import hmac
import json
import time
from unittest.mock import patch

import redis
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import select

import app.database
import app.main
from app.celery_worker import celery
from app.models.customer import Customer
from app.models.webhook_event import WebhookEvent
from app.services.webhook_handler import process_github_webhook_task


class BrokenBrokerTask:
    def apply_async(self, args, queue):
        # The task still uses Celery/Kombu's real publish path. Only its broker
        # connection points at a reserved, unbound loopback port for this call.
        with celery.connection_for_write("redis://127.0.0.1:56380/1") as connection:
            return process_github_webhook_task.apply_async(
                args=args, queue=queue, connection=connection, retry=False
            )


def main():
    with app.database.SessionLocal() as db:
        customer = Customer(tenant_id="qa-broker-failure", name="Broker QA", webhook_secret="qa-broker-secret", allowed_event_types=[])
        db.add(customer)
        db.commit()
        customer_id = customer.id

    body = json.dumps({"action": "opened", "sender": {"login": "qa"}, "repository": {"full_name": "qa/broker"}}).encode()
    headers = {
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "X-Hub-Signature-256": "sha256=" + hmac.new(b"qa-broker-secret", body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest(),
        "X-GitHub-Delivery": "qa-broker-retry",
    }
    path = "/webhooks/qa-broker-failure/github"
    key = "webhook:idempotency:qa-broker-failure:github:qa-broker-retry"
    r = redis.Redis.from_url("redis://127.0.0.1:56379/0")
    with TestClient(app.main.app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
        with patch("app.main.get_task", return_value=BrokenBrokerTask()):
            failed = client.post(path, content=body, headers=headers)
        assert failed.status_code == 500, failed.text
        assert not r.exists(key)
        print("REAL_BROKER_FAILURE_HTTP=500")
        print("RESERVATION_AFTER_FAILURE=absent")

        retried = client.post(path, content=body, headers=headers)
        assert retried.status_code == 202, retried.text
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            with app.database.SessionLocal() as db:
                events = db.scalars(select(WebhookEvent).where(WebhookEvent.customer_id == customer_id, WebhookEvent.event_id == "qa-broker-retry")).all()
                if len(events) == 1 and events[0].status == "PROCESSED":
                    break
            time.sleep(0.2)
        else:
            raise AssertionError("retry not processed by actual worker")
        assert r.exists(key)
        print("RETRY_HTTP=202")
        print("RETRY_PERSISTED=one PROCESSED row")
    r.close()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Probe the real Celery worker failure hook on QA-only services."""

import time
import uuid

from app.services.webhook_handler import process_github_webhook_task


result = process_github_webhook_task.apply_async(
    args=[str(uuid.uuid4()), {"action": "opened"}, "qa-invalid-payload"],
    queue="high_priority",
)
deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
while time.monotonic() < deadline and not result.ready():
    time.sleep(0.2)
assert result.ready(), "real worker did not finish invalid task"
assert result.state == "FAILURE", (result.state, str(result.result))
print(f"TASK_ID={result.id}")
print(f"TASK_STATE={result.state}")
print(f"FAILURE_CLASS={type(result.result).__name__}")
